internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: A divinely-inflicted defeat that brings God's active opponents low — checking/thwarting their aim and abasing them — while leaving them alive (explicitly short of destroying or killing them).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all three verbal tokens (Form I, active and passive), k-b-t names something God does to those who oppose Him and His Messenger: it brings them low. In 3:127 the imperfect active يَكْبِتَهُمْ is set by أَوْ against لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا ('cut off a portion'), i.e. it is the non-lethal alternative to destroying a group, and its result-clause فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ shows survivors turning back thwarted/empty-handed. In 58:5 the two passives كُبِتُوا۟ / كُبِتَ assert a recurring pattern ('as those before them were') against the muḥāddūn, adjacent to a separately-promised عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ. The single field account 'humiliating bring-low of God's opponents, short of destruction' covers all three; whether the finer emphasis is dynamic thwarting (3:127) or settled abasement (58:5) is not arbitrated by the corpus.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: kbt does NOT entail killing/annihilation (in 3:127 it is disjoined by أَوْ from قَطْع طَرَف and its patients survive to retreat); it is NOT identical to the frustration it causes (خَآئِبِينَ, root ḫyb, is the effect, kbt the cause); it is NOT the promised humiliating punishment (عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ, root hwn, stands in a separate additional clause); and it is NOT agent-neutral or generic humiliation — the agent is always God (active subject in 3:127, divine passive in 58:5) and the patient is always an active opponent of God (kuffār, muḥāddūn), never a believer or neutral party.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 3:127:7:1 يَكْبِتَهُمْ is coordinated by أَوْ with لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا and yields فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ — a dynamic, non-lethal battlefield thwarting whose foregrounded content is frustration/repulse, not disgrace. This decisively refutes any 'kbt = kill/destroy' gloss (establishing the ≠ annihilation boundary) and simultaneously resists an 'abasement-primary' nucleus, since the salient outcome here is being foiled and turned back, not being disgraced.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: That kbt is simply 'to disgrace/abase/humiliate' (leaning on the مُّهِين collocation and the opponents-of-God patients in 58:5), treating خَآئِبِينَ as incidental. Rejected as the core because it under-reads 3:127, where the أَوْ-alternation to قَطْع and the خَآئِبِينَ result make thwarting/repulse the salient content. Its mirror ('to thwart/rout' as the core) is rejected symmetrically because it under-reads 58:5's abasement framing. The narrowest single account surviving both verse-events is the bridged field sense 'humiliating bring-low short of destruction' — but which facet is primary remains underdetermined on a 2-context base.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three analysts (A, B, C) converge on MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE. The evidence is internally CONSISTENT, adversarially clean (hard ≠ kill boundary, single divine agent, single opponent-patient type, no lexicalized/nominal sub-class — all tokens are Form I verbs), which rules out WEAK/UNRESOLVED and supports a PREFERRED field account. STRONG/UNIVERSAL is affirmatively barred on breadth: 3 tokens collapse to 2 independent contexts (58:5's pair is bound by an internal كَمَا equation asserting one event-type), a single POS, and no morphological spread. A genuine residual facet-tension (dynamic thwart in 3:127 vs. settled abasement in 58:5, tracked by active-imperfect vs. passive-perfect voice and by non-kbt co-text words that associate but cannot define) caps confidence: the finer nucleus is underdetermined even though the broad field account is not resisted by any token. Hence PREFERRED field account at MODERATE, with the sub-nucleus split recorded rather than forced.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B structural, C adversarial) converged on the same field account, the same ≠ kill boundary, and the same thwart-vs-abase underdetermination and MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.
candidate_root_contribution: A divinely-inflicted defeat that brings God's active opponents low — checking/thwarting their aim and abasing them — while leaving them alive (explicitly short of destroying or killing them).

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 3 confirmed verbal tokens: active imperfect يَكْبِتَهُمْ (3:127:7:1); passive perfects كُبِتُوا۟ (58:5:6:1) and كُبِتَ (58:5:8:1), the latter pair bound by كَمَا within one verse.
layer_attribution.derivation: All Form I (qac_verb_form=null; 'V' = POS Verb, not derived Form V); active/passive voice alternants of one transitive triliteral verb — no nominal, participial, or augmented-form spread.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: No lexicalized or nominal sub-class exists; the root is attested only as a finite verb, so grading is not capped by a resistant lexicalized class but by breadth and the facet tension.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Co-text supplies associated but non-defining roots: خَآئِبِينَ (ḫyb, effect of kbt in 3:127), عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ (hwn, separate punishment in 58:5), قَطْع طَرَف (qṭʿ, the أَوْ-disjoined lethal alternative). These contextual/narrative facts inform boundaries but are kept out of the root claim itself.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary voice-tracked split (active→thwart, passive→abase) is reconciled into one field nucleus ('humiliating bring-low short of destruction') that no token resists; the finer nucleus is left explicitly unresolved rather than forced, and recorded as two adversarial boundaries.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: Residual, non-fatal: whether the definitional center is dynamic thwarting (3:127) or settled abasement (58:5) is unarbitrated on 2 independent contexts; this mutual facet-resistance caps strength at MODERATE / scope at REPRESENTATIVE.

hard_cases.reason: Its أَوْ-disjunction from لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا and result فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ both fix the ≠ annihilation boundary and foreground dynamic thwarting, resisting an abasement-primary nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: 3:127:7:1 يَكْبِتَهُمْ is coordinated by أَوْ with لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا and yields فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ — a dynamic, non-lethal battlefield thwarting whose foregrounded content is frustration/repulse, not disgrace.

hard_cases.reason: Its مُّهِين + كَمَا-predecessors framing foregrounds settled abasement, resisting a thwart-in-battle-only nucleus and forming the mirror pole of the underdetermination.

evidence_basis.statement: 58:5 frames kbt as an already-accomplished humiliating downfall of opposers, distinct from and prior to the separately-promised humiliating punishment.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No token finally RESISTS the broad field account, so there is no RESISTANT_SEAM. But two genuine adversarial boundaries are evidence-derived: 3:127 fixes the ≠ kill boundary and the dynamic-thwart pole, while 58:5 supplies the abasement pole. Their mutual resistance to each other's narrow nucleus is the recorded residual tension that caps strength at MODERATE; both statements also appear in the cluster supporting-evidence notes and the strongest_counterexample.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A kbt occurrence whose agent is not God, or whose patient is a believer or a neutral (non-adversarial) party, or one that denotes actual killing/annihilation rather than a survivable bring-low.
rejection_condition.search_location: Both attested contexts (3:127 battle disjunction; 58:5 muḥāddūn comparison) plus any newly surfaced kbt token; inspect agent, patient class, and whether the patients survive/retreat.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Check voice and the syntactic subject/agent, the identity of the patient (kuffār/muḥāddūn vs. others), and the result-clause (survival + retreat as in فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ vs. elimination); compare against the أَوْ-disjunction from قَطْع طَرَف that marks the non-lethal boundary.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish kbt itself from the co-text roots that only associate: ḫyb (خَآئِبِينَ, the effect), hwn (مُّهِين, the separate punishment), qṭʿ (قَطْع طَرَف, the disjoined lethal alternative). A finding grounded in those roots' semantics rather than kbt's own distribution does not count.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such an occurrence is found, the 'divine-agent, opponent-patient, non-lethal' field account is falsified or must be narrowed, and the root would drop to WEAK/UNRESOLVED or require re-partition.

reopen_conditions: If a kbt token appears with a non-divine agent, or directed at a believer/neutral party rather than an opponent of God (kuffār/muḥāddūn), reopen the 'divine-agent, opponent-patient' restriction.

If a kbt occurrence surfaces in a context that foregrounds neither thwarting (khayba / inqilāb) nor abasement (muhīn / hawn), thereby arbitrating the 3:127-vs-58:5 facet split, reopen the thwart-vs-abase underdetermination and re-grade toward STRONG or a partition.

A full adversarial refutation returning SUPPORTED is not affirmatively claimed (NOT_RUN rather than PASSED) because the finer nucleus is underdetermined on only 2 independent contexts: 3:127 and 58:5 mutually resist each other's narrow reading. No occurrence fails the core, so status is NOT_RUN with the residual facet-tension recorded, not FAILED.
